claim: Two builds of the same source (a: unmodified; b: one comment-only line appended) with different DSO digests must have identical analysis identity and identical reachable sets. Equality is the stability criterion.

identity_recomputation.when: 2026-10-29, after P0-A extended the identity; the closures were NOT re-run
identity_recomputation.method: construct each module's DsoGraph and call analysis_identity; only libcrypto.so.3 is the candidate module in both closures
identity_recomputation.basis: sha256 over, in module-name order, each module name and a canonical JSON input record: every allocated (SHF_ALLOC) section's (name, ELF type, virtual address, size, sha256 of its bytes), the sorted relocation table (section, section-relative offset, type, canonical symbol, addend), the sorted [name, addr, size, kind] defined-symbol rows, the sorted dynamic-symbol rows, and the loader entries (SONAME/NEEDED/RUNPATH/RPATH). Required minimum sections: .text, .plt, .plt.got, .init, .fini, .rodata, .data, .data.rel.ro, .data.rel.ro.local, .got, .got.plt, .init_array, .fini_array; NOBITS sections (address/size only): .bss. Excluded: .debug_*, .zdebug_*, .comment, .note*, .gnu_debuglink, .gnu_debugaltlink, .gnu.build.attributes, every non-allocated section (SHF_ALLOC is absent). ``.llvm.<hash>`` and ``@@VERSION`` suffixes are canonicalised as in the symbol table; the DSO file digest is recorded as a non-identity.
identity_recomputation.note: the reachable-set fields in a/b are the original closures and are retained unchanged: the reachability algorithm did not change in P0-A or P0-B, and the new identity was computed without re-running those closures

negative_control.summary: a scratch copy of the v1p libcrypto with one .data.rel.ro dispatch-slot relocation addend patched 0x493990 -> 0x160c80 keeps .text and the defined-symbol table byte-identical, changes the analysis identity, and adds 0x160c80 to the targeted build_graph upper bound

note: The raw-name digest differs only by build-dependent .llvm.<hash> suffixes on otherwise identical addresses and canonical names; the canonical digest is the identity.
